text:
marco: hey folks, first week here! quick question about developer API keys and sandbox use. i'm wiring up CI to call the hosted API and want to avoid hitting limits or leaking keys. what are the practical defaults for sandbox rate limits (requests/min, concurrency, token throughput)? any CI best practices?

devex: welcome, marco :wave: defaults are conservative for new projects (often ~60 reqs/min, low concurrent sockets). token throughput throttling can kick in for heavy streaming responses. for CI: use ephemeral keys, set strict max_tokens, and pin the model. what's your expected QPS and token output?

marco: thanks! test will be from a single runner at ~20 rps for 2 minutes, responses ~400 tokens.

infra-ops: that should be fine. short bursts under 30 rps rarely get blocked. if you plan sustained load or bigger tokens, file a quota request in Console -> Usage -> Quota Requests. include project id, time window, and CIDR for IP allowlist if needed.

marco: good to know. how do we create ephemeral keys? can they be scoped to read-only or to a specific model?

tayla: use Console -> API Keys -> Create Key -> Ephemeral. set expiry (1-6h) and minimal scopes. you can limit to model access in the key metadata; also rotate per-job if you want stronger isolation.

marco: any tips for handling 429s in CI? i want tests to be robust but fail-fast if infra is the problem.

infra-ops: add exponential backoff with jitter and fail after N retries. also respect Retry-After header when present. for tests that assert latency, don't retry silently; surface failures.

ops-bot: notice: project:zeta-dev showing recent 429 spikes yesterday. open a ticket if you expect higher sustained load.

marco: appreciated. sample curl for our scripts?

devex: simple example (cap tokens and model):

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"open-redwood-1-small","input":"smoke test","max_tokens":400}'

marco: perfect. one last thing: are sandbox keys audited in logs? i'm paranoid about leaking in CI logs.

tayla: keys show up as masked in Console logs; treat them as secrets. use CI secret stores (do not echo env vars) and add log scrubbing for any accidental prints. ephemeral keys help reduce blast radius.

onboarding-bot: reminder: new-hires checklist item "Create ephemeral sandbox key" assigned to @marco is still open.

marco: done, created ephemeral key expiring in 3h and updated CI. i'll file a quota request if we need to expand. thanks for the help!
